header:
Date: 2025-12-31
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Erin Park (DataWave CTO), Marcus Li (DataWave Infra), Priya Nair (DataWave Security), Nora Ahmed (DataWave MLOps)
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Main topics: networking/routing issues preventing e2e inference, planned OS/GPU driver upgrade, ingress/egress and certificate concerns, and next steps for tests and maintenance window. Action items assigned for network screenshots, driver checklist, and security docs.
topics: Upgrade plan: OS and GPU drivers
Ingress/NAT and egress for telemetry and model downloads
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy almost new year, we'll keep this tight 30-45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:06] Erin: Erin here, Marcus, Priya and Nora on my side.
[00:10] Luis: Luis here from Redwood, I'll handle the infra troubleshooting parts.
[00:13] Samira: Awesome. Quick recap from last week, Marcus you were going to try the route table change and send screenshots, did that happen?
[00:22] Marcus: Uh, so we tried, we — we updated the route to point to the peer but we saw traffic still drop, I think there's an NAT behavior on the transit VPC that's intercepting packets, so not fully green.
[00:34] Samira: Got it. Can you describe the path? like... public internet or through transit?
[00:38] Marcus: It's through our transit VPC, we have a central firewall that does egress inspection, it rewrites some source IPs for outbound, maybe that's confusing the 443 health checks to Redwood's control plane.
[00:51] Luis: That's consistent with what we saw in the logs — the pilot nodes try to fetch model shards and the control plane gets a mismatched source. We added a recommended SNAT exemption but it might not be applied across the transit VPC.
[01:05] Priya: Just to flag, any change that opens unmanaged egress is a no-go for us, we need approved routes and audit logging.
[01:11] Samira: Totally understood. The plan we proposed was to use a managed NAT with static egress IPs plus an allowlist on your firewall. That avoids changing wide route tables.
[01:20] Erin: Can you re-share the allowlist IPs? we haven't seen the updated spreadsheet with static IPs yet.
[01:25] Samira: I'll paste after the call; Luis will also put the IP list into the Confluence security doc.
[01:29] Nora: One note, we still had a model download time spike — like 30% slower on the private nodes versus the hosted baseline, wondering if kernel or driver versions are misaligned.
[01:39] Luis: Yeah, that could be CUDA mismatch or image misconfig. We're seeing the pilot AMI is on Ubuntu 20.04 with CUDA 11.4, we recommend Ubuntu 22.04 and CUDA 12.1 for the newer drivers, especially for the A100 equivalent we have in the pilot.
[01:52] Marcus: Ok, we were holding off on OS upgrades because of internal change freeze, but if drivers are the root cause we can schedule a maintenance window.
[01:59] Samira: For minimal disruption we'd do a rolling upgrade, cordon one node at a time, run smoke tests. We'll provide the exact driver/AMI checklist.
[02:07] Priya: Also need to confirm how key management will work — we're using our KMS and need to know if Redwood's Private will call out to our key vault or if keys are pre-provisioned in the node.
[02:17] Luis: For the Private VPC option the control plane talks to your KMS over a secure peered connection, and the node can be configured to use customer-managed keys. There might be a handshake step we need to script.
[02:27] Erin: Is that documented in the security whitepaper, or is that a custom step?
[02:31] Samira: We have a KMS integration doc — I'll link it. It covers both KMS+HSM and the fallback if you want Redwood-managed but encrypted keys.
[02:41] Marcus: Back to the routing — I'll export the transit firewall logs and send them, the SNAT exemption is a request to the security team managing the transit VPC.
[02:49] Nora: For the model slowdowns, I can run the perf script that Redwood provided. I ran one last week but with older image config; I'll re-run with the suggested AMI once Luis shares it.
[02:59] Luis: Great. Also one more note: we observed occasional 502s when the KV cache warmed up after restarts, that's likely due to TCP idle timeouts on the NLB. We recommend setting the idle timeout to 3600s for long-lived KV connections.
[03:11] Erin: Where do we change that?
[03:13] Luis: On the Load Balancer config in your cloud console — we'll send an example terraform snippet.
[03:19] Samira: On the security front, Priya, you mentioned certificate rotation concerns last week?
[03:23] Priya: Yes, need to ensure whatever cert rotation process you use doesn't break long-lived model connections. We need clarity if Redwood calls a renewal endpoint or if we manage cert rollout via our PKI.
[03:36] Samira: Either works — typically customers prefer to manage PKI and we support cert hot-reload on the nodes. We'll test rotation in the maintenance window.
[03:45] Marcus: About fallback: if private nodes can't serve a request do we have automatic routing to hosted Redwood endpoints? we want graceful degradation.
[03:52] Luis: There's a built-in fallback policy, but to enable it we need to set routing policy in the pilot config and whitelist the hosted endpoints in your firewall for outbound. It's opt-in.
[04:01] Erin: That seems reasonable. We'll need to document which endpoints are contacted for telemetry too.
[04:06] Samira: We'll send a telemetry endpoints list and retention details.
[04:10] Nora: Quick question — is there a plan to upgrade the model to the newer quantized variant? we noticed memory pressure on inference.
[04:17] Luis: We suggested a q4_0 quantized variant for lower memory with a small quality delta. We can run side-by-side A/B to measure latency and quality.
[04:26] Nora: Cool, I'd like that as part of the benchmark matrix.
[04:29] Samira: OK adding it to the test plan. Next, maintenance window — Marcus, what dates are blackouts?
[04:36] Marcus: Jan 1-2 is blackout, after that we have Jan 6 as a light day, Jan 7 is open.
[04:42] Samira: We'll propose Jan 6 for the rolling driver upgrade. Luis will own the runbook and we will schedule a dry-run on Jan 5 in a canary subnet.
[04:51] Priya: Make sure the dry-run logs go to our audit bucket with immutable retention for compliance.
[04:56] Samira: Noted. We'll set immutable retention and share details.
[04:59] Erin: Any blockers on our side?
[05:02] Marcus: Just the SNAT exemption and we need the static egress IP list.
[05:07] Luis: We'll give the IP list and a terraform snippet to create the NAT with elastic IPs.
[05:12] Samira: OK let's recap action items, I'll speak slowly. Samira will share security doc and IP list; Luis will share AMI/driver checklist and terraform for idle timeout; Marcus will send firewall logs and confirm SNAT exemption; Priya will share PKI owners; Nora will run updated benchmarks. Everyone good?
[05:31] Erin: Yep. Thanks.
[05:33] Samira: Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and schedule invite for maintenance. Happy new year.
[05:39] End of meeting
